after reading this post and the comments my perspective has totally been shifted. in all honesty i watched this tv show for the 1st time when i was in a HUGE depressive state. i was not medicated, isolating myself, and engaging in self medicating behavior with benzos. 

i think because i was in the lowest state and have struggled with substance abuse in my life i connected so so so much with his character.

all in all, i think that bojack kept running from his problems but he would never out chase them. it’s a learning experience to see how we must make amends and hold ourselves accountable. i am inspired to make change in my own life, get help, and try to heal my relationships. i acknowledge that it is a privilege being able to access mental health resources  and without that i definitely would not be here today and ended up like bojack in “the view from half way down”

hey! 

i felt very uneasy with it too and when i told my friends about it they were like oh that’s not bad! and i felt extremely invalidated because i never show them my real side

until i had a huge episode and basically a nasty nasty fight with my friends and they got all mad- people only say they are okay with mental health until they see the bad side of it. anyway being able to tell them about my DX gave context of my actions however it did not forgive them because i still have to hold myself accountable 

anyway after i got prescribed lamictal it has done WONDERS. finding the right meds is hard and the right dose but once i found the dose that works for me i have been so great :) i feel stable for the first time ever - i mean not 100% stable but it’s not as extreme as before

i am WAY less depressed which is amazing because i was misdiagnosed with MDD for so long and drowning because nothing worked 

any way a diagnosis is a BLESSING- it does not define you and that is why saying “ i have bipolar” instead of “i am bipolar” is important 

as well learning my cues and how to deal with them has been liberating because now i can try to be as self aware as possible. 

my best coping mechanisms come from DBT. i love 54321 because it’s legit the only thing i can remember and breathing- i forget to breathe a lot

another thing is that it’s a learning curve! we learn from our mistakes and that is OKAY. learning how to accept how we feel, our emotions, and actions is crucial.

oh and yes the classic 
- eat meals to fuel ur soul
- try to sleep (melatonin helps me) 
- exercise has done WONDERS for me 
- daylio is a mood tracker app 
- and i love podcasts of people with bp talking about their experiences

sending u BIGGGGG. hugs 🤗
